verdict.rationale: 2FAS has no dedicated sync server to self-host, but 2FAS Pass documents syncing its encrypted vault to a user-run WebDAV endpoint, and the pricing page advertises 'Freedom to self-host your data'. That lets an admin keep Pass vault data on their own infrastructure. 2FAS Auth sync is documented only for iCloud and Google Drive, so authenticator secrets would leave the perimeter. Missing for 10: a self-hostable first-party sync server, self-hosted sync for 2FAS Auth tokens, admin deployment documentation, and independent corroboration of a self-hosted setup.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the sync server on my own infrastructure and keep every secret inside my perimeter

citations.quote: Use the following instructions if you have synchronized 2FAS Pass Vault with your WebDAV.
You decide where to store your Items. You can store it in your own cloud or keep it as an encrypted file on an external drive.
